bad.title: Continue shopping pulls as hard
bad.text: The same filled blue as Check out, so it reads like the next step too.

bad.title: Check out only wins by reading
bad.text: With two equal buttons, people read both labels before they know which one ends the order.

good.title: Continue shopping steps back
good.text: Plain text, still one click away for people who want to keep browsing.

good.title: Check out is the one filled button
good.text: The way to pay the €67 shows up in a glance.

bad.title: Cancel what, the upload or this
bad.text: On its own, it could stop the photos or just close something.
bad.wait: Press Upload 3 photos to see this.

bad.title: Cancel here keeps uploading
bad.text: People who want to cancel the upload press Cancel, and it carries on.
bad.wait: Press Upload 3 photos, then Cancel, to see this.

bad.title: OK is the one that stops it
bad.text: Nothing on it says stop, so people reread “Cancel upload?” to be sure.
bad.wait: Press Upload 3 photos, then Cancel, to see this.

good.title: Stop upload names what stops
good.text: Clear on its own, even with three photos half sent.
good.wait: Press Upload 3 photos to see this.

good.title: Keep uploading is the way back
good.text: It says what happens next, so nobody presses it to stop.
good.wait: Press Upload 3 photos, then Stop upload, to see this.

good.title: Same words as the button pressed
good.text: Stop upload twice, so people know they’re confirming what they asked for.
good.wait: Press Upload 3 photos, then Stop upload, to see this.

bad.title: Save sits one button over
bad.text: A hand that reaches for the usual spot lands on Delete folder.

bad.title: Delete folder dressed as Save
bad.text: Same filled blue, same size, in the spot where Save usually goes.

bad.title: Gone, with no way back
bad.text: One fast click removes 24 files shared with 5 people.
bad.wait: Press Delete folder to see this.

good.title: Save has the last spot alone
good.text: A habit click there only ever saves.

good.title: Delete folder out at the far left
good.text: A red outline and the width of the bar between it and Save.

good.title: Undo for six seconds
good.text: If a slip gets through, the folder and its 24 files come back in one click.
good.wait: Press Delete folder to see this.

bad.title: Phone looks filled in
bad.text: +351 912 345 67 is one digit short, and nothing points to it.

bad.title: Pressing Book table does nothing
bad.text: No message and no cursor move, so people recheck the name, the date and the time.

good.title: The cursor lands in Phone
good.text: People can type the missing digit straight away.
good.wait: Press Book table to see this.

good.title: Book table can still be pressed
good.text: Pressing it is how people find out what’s missing.

good.title: The message counts the digits
good.text: It needs 9 after +351 and this one has 8, so the fix is plain.
good.wait: Press Book table to see this.

bad.title: Crop hides behind a frame icon
bad.text: It’s the last of three, so people try Layers and Adjust first.

bad.title: Every wrong guess opens a panel
bad.text: Each miss shows a tool people didn’t ask for, and the count goes up.
bad.wait: Pick a tool to see this.

good.title: Crop says Crop
good.text: People go straight to it, without opening Layers or Adjust.

good.title: Found on the first try
good.text: The word does the work, so there’s nothing to guess.

good.title: Close stays a bare ×
good.text: One of the few icons everyone reads, so it needs no word.

bad.title: Save a copy is fifth of ten
bad.text: A folder icon, the same size and weight as Bookmarks and Properties.

bad.title: No groups, no gaps
bad.text: Zoom, export and settings run together, so people scan all ten every time.

bad.title: Each hover is one more check
bad.text: The count shows how many icons people read before finding the save.

good.title: The main action gets a word
good.text: Save a copy is the only label in the row, so the eye goes there first.

good.title: A divider closes the zoom set
good.text: Zoom in, Zoom out and Fit to page read as one group people can skip.

good.title: Five rare actions behind More
good.text: Each one has a word here, and none of them crowd the row.

bad.title: + is smaller than a fingertip
bad.text: One tap covers Play and Close too, so it’s a guess which one fires.

bad.title: Close sits right against +
bad.text: A tap a little to the right closes the player instead of adding the song.

good.title: + is as wide as a fingertip
good.text: At 40 px, a tap that lands a little off still adds the song.

good.title: Close gets extra room
good.text: More space than between Play and +, so a slip toward it lands on nothing.

bad.title: Delete looks safe to open in a tab
bad.text: People open links in a new tab just to look, and that alone deletes Home.

bad.title: The address ends in /delete
bad.text: The only warning, down in the status bar where few people look.

bad.title: Deleted, with no Undo
bad.text: Back to addresses only returns to the list, now without Home.

good.title: Delete has no address to open
good.text: A button can’t be opened in a tab, so people press it on purpose.

good.title: Edit stays a link
good.text: Opening it in a new tab is harmless, since it only shows a form.

good.title: Undo right after the delete
good.text: For five seconds, a slip brings Home back in one click.

bad.title: No new tab, no address to show
bad.text: Ctrl-click just swaps this tab, and hovering shows nowhere it leads.

bad.title: The address stays on /week
bad.text: After Open agenda, there’s still nothing to bookmark or share for the agenda.

bad.title: Back has nothing to go back to
bad.text: The swap adds no history, so people can’t return to the week.

good.title: Opens in a new tab like any link
good.text: Ctrl-click keeps the week in this tab and the agenda in the next.

good.title: Hover shows where it leads
good.text: calendar.example.com/team-sync/agenda, before anyone clicks.
good.wait: Hover Open agenda to see this.

good.title: Back returns to the week
good.text: After opening the agenda, one press brings the calendar back.

bad.title: Blue is the only clue
bad.text: With color blindness or a dim screen, cleanup guide reads as part of the sentence.

bad.title: Grayscale makes both links vanish
bad.text: Turn it on, and nothing marks cleanup guide or compare plans.

good.title: An underline marks cleanup guide
good.text: It reads as a link without relying on color.

good.title: Both links survive grayscale
good.text: Turn it on, and the underlines still show where to click.
